newsitem.title: INDIA: Key politician quits India's ruling alliance.
newsitem.headline: Key politician quits India's ruling alliance.

text.p: A key member of India's ruling United Front alliance switched back to the Congress party on Tuesday in a move that could foreshadow trouble for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's fragile coalition, politicians said.
Former Civil Aviation Minister Madhavrao Scindia told a news conference he was returning to the Congress after an emotional meeting with party president Sitaram Kesri.
Scindia was expelled from the Congress party by former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao after he accused Rao of framing him in a money-laundering scandal earlier this year.
"I was expelled from the Congress. There was a design. It is all in the past now," Scindia said during a joint news conference with Kesri.
Kesri hugged Scindia and described their meeting as "the return of a long-lost brother".
Kesri succeeded Rao as Congress leader in September, when the former prime minister resigned as party president after being named in a cheating case.
Rao's 1991-96 tenure as prime minister saw the exit of several ministers -- some charged with corruption, others forced out over political differences.
Their departure played a role in Congress' worst-ever defeat in general elections in April and May, which forced Rao and the party out of power.
Kesri's leadership has raised the party's hopes of wooing back most of the Congress leaders who had defected.
"This could be a serious development for the Deve Gowda government," a senior politician from Gowda's 13-group United Front coalition told Reuters.
"Scindia alone is no threat but other Congress members coming together could spell trouble," the politician said.
A Congress party resolution on Monday emphasised the return of former colleagues as an important goal for the party.
Party officials say one group that Kesri was keen to invite back to the fold was Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress.
The group broke away from the Congress party following differences between Chidambaram and Rao over their rival electoral allies in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
Congress, holding the balance of power in a hung parliament, warned Deve Gowda on Monday against ignoring its interests but said it had no immediate plans to pull down his government.

The scandal-plagued Congress party also decided that senior leaders of its key decision-making Congress Working Committee (CWC) would disclose their financial assets shortly to spruce up the party's image, which has been tarnished by a string of corruption cases.
"The developments of the past five months have raised a number of questions in the minds of Congress' rank-and-file by the actions and utterances of the United Front leaders," the resolution said.

"Congress calls upon the United Front to change its attitude and, instead of hurling abuses at the Congress, take corrective steps... CWC will continue to review the situation as and when it develops," it added.

The resolution also criticised the United Front for what it called poor economic management and blamed the coalition for failing to win a vote for a place on the United Nations Security Council last month.
